name: Project-S
description: The rapid increase in space debris, especially fragments between 1-10 cm, threatens satellites and future missions. With over 900,000 such objects in orbit, collision risks are rising, driving up costs and endangering space sustainability. Current ground-based and optical tracking methods are limited by atmospheric interference, line-of-sight constraints, and inefficiency in dark orbital regions. Project-S addresses this challenge with an AI-driven, radar-based detection system on a cost-effective CubeSat platform. Unlike optical or ground-based systems, our active microwave radar operates in all conditions, detecting debris too small for traditional methods. AI-powered onboard processing ensures real-time tracking, while ground-based deep learning refines data for enhanced accuracy.

name: QOODA
description: The heavy reliance of modern navigation on GNSS (GPS, Galileo) has some major weaknesses, like interference, spoofing, and signal jamming, which present a serious challenge for aerospace, autonomous systems, and critical infrastructure. Quantum magnetic anomaly navigation (Quantum MagANav), which uses highly sensitive quantum sensors to navigate using the Earth's unique magnetic “fingerprints,” offers a robust alternative. However, its effectiveness is severely compromised or even rendered impossible by the low resolution and accuracy of current magnetic anomaly maps.

name: Qoro Quantum
description: Quantum computing has the potential to significantly advance various fields, including simulation, optimization, and machine learning. However, realizing this potential requires large-scale, robust quantum computers. While building scalable monolithic quantum systems presents fundamental challenges, modular quantum architectures offer a solution. These modular systems, however, introduce new complexities in networking and orchestration. Qoro Quantum addresses these complexities by developing a network stack that automates the parallelization and orchestration of quantum algorithm execution across networked computing devices, including hybrid classical-quantum systems that integrate quantum computing with high-performance computing (HPC). Our solution enhances the execution of quantum algorithms on real devices, accelerating the timeline for unlocking quantum computing’s full capabilities.
